title: Shakespeare complained about a muddy nine men's morris board in 1595 - Millfall is that same board game in pixel art, where closing a mill executes a piece
text: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Titania complains that "the nine men's morris is fill'd up with mud" - the village board rained out, around 1595. The mill game picked up a name almost everywhere it landed: merels in England, Mühle in Germany, malom in Hungary, morabaraba in southern Africa. Millfall is that classic board game reimagined in pixel art - same nine pieces, same mills, same flying endgame - except closing a mill doesn't just remove an enemy piece, it executes it, one of 33 death animations. The card above was rendered in-engine in the Frost Hollow arena.

title: Millfall has a witness raven that calls out every execution in this nine men's morris indie game - poke it six times in four seconds and it stops narrating to complain about you
text: Every arena has the same witness: a raven on one perch, watching the whole battle and naming each execution as it happens. It wears a different coat in every arena - this is the Ember Forge, so it hisses instead of cawing. The complaint is a real reaction in the game, not a mock-up: six pokes inside four seconds and it stops narrating to file one. Recorded in-engine. Nine men's morris as an abstract strategy PC game in pixel art.
